findings.claim: authenticate passes the raw token to audit.log before validating it, so every credential presented, valid or not, goes unredacted to the logger that CONTRACT.md says is persisted. This breaks the contract rule that bearer credentials must never be written to logs. The code does not use the word 'bearer'; I treat the token as a bearer credential because it is the value authenticate validates. The code was read, not executed.
findings.cause: authenticate audit logging: raw token is passed to the persisted audit logger before validation

findings.claim: The only test is a vacuous witness for the logging contract. It asserts only authenticate's return value and never observes what reaches audit.log, so it would stay green with the credential leak in place. It also has no rejected-token case. As checked in, the test file declares or imports neither assert nor authenticate, and the checkout has no setup file that supplies them, so it cannot exercise the real entry point unless the environment injects those names.
findings.cause: authenticate test witness: assertion checks only the return value and never observes audit logger output

findings.claim: src/unit.js uses audit and validate but neither declares nor imports them, and no other source file or setup file in the checkout defines them. Because the file is an ES module, authenticate throws ReferenceError at audit.log unless the runtime injects a global audit, and the same applies to validate. The throw is inferred from reading the code, since no lane or test was run. If this holds at runtime, the checkout does not deliver a working authenticate, and the test's expected true return cannot be reached.
findings.cause: authenticate call: audit and validate are referenced without any declaration or import in the module

reasons: The range contains one source line that sends the token to audit.log, which directly conflicts with CONTRACT.md's ban on logging bearer credentials to a persisted logger.
